The stated levelsA background with more than one languageProficiency and specialist workKeeping the record useful

Urdu, Punjabi, and Hindi, with the individual proficiency levels recorded on my profile.

  • My LinkedIn language record lists Urdu and Punjabi at native or bilingual proficiency, and Hindi at full professional proficiency. These are the labels recorded on the profile reviewed on 6 October 2026. The portfolio retains each label rather than grouping all three under one uniform claim.
  • As a Pakistani student living in Saudi Arabia, my wider profile combines different linguistic and educational contexts. This language record is one part of that background. It sits alongside my English-medium public writing and my current International A Level studies.
  • The labels here are self-reported profile levels. They are not presented as qualifications in translation or interpretation. A specialist task, including legal or technical communication, can require vocabulary, methods, and professional standards beyond a general language label.
  • The language hub provides the complete table, including the lower proficiency levels for other languages. This allows a reader to see the whole record without assuming equal ability across it.
01 / 04

The stated levels

My LinkedIn language record lists Urdu and Punjabi at native or bilingual proficiency, and Hindi at full professional proficiency.

These are the labels recorded on the profile reviewed on 6 October 2026. The portfolio retains each label rather than grouping all three under one uniform claim.

The connection

A language profile is most useful when it gives an accurate starting point for a conversation.

Read the deeper context+

These entries form the established-language group in my record. They are separate from the working and elementary languages described on the other pages.

02 / 04

A background with more than one language

As a Pakistani student living in Saudi Arabia, my wider profile combines different linguistic and educational contexts.

This language record is one part of that background. It sits alongside my English-medium public writing and my current International A Level studies.

The connection

Speaking more than one language can make differences in phrasing and perspective more noticeable.

Read the deeper context+

My aim is to communicate with attention to the setting and the person reading or listening, rather than assume that the same wording works equally well in every context.

03 / 04

Proficiency and specialist work

The labels here are self-reported profile levels.

They are not presented as qualifications in translation or interpretation. A specialist task, including legal or technical communication, can require vocabulary, methods, and professional standards beyond a general language label.

The connection

I do not claim to provide professional translation or legal interpretation in these languages.

Read the deeper context+

For a practical conversation, the subject, format, and level of detail still matter. Keeping that distinction clear makes the profile more useful than relying on a language count alone.

04 / 04

Keeping the record useful

The language hub provides the complete table, including the lower proficiency levels for other languages.

This allows a reader to see the whole record without assuming equal ability across it.

The connection

Future evidence could add more context through demonstrated writing, an identified assessment, or actual tasks.

Read the deeper context+

Until then, the portfolio presents the profile labels faithfully and avoids assigning invented scores or credentials. The purpose is clarity about the current record and room for it to develop.

Source context

Profile facts were reviewed on 6 October 2026. Expanded prose provides personal and learning context; listed achievements remain separate from future ambitions.
